rationale:
Evidence. Iteration 3 (kp 2.5, sensor_size 0.016, base_speed 1.3, kd 0.3, weights [2,1,0,-1,-2], last_direction) is the best raced design at 159.2. The race still ended every run off_track. max_error stayed at 0.0606 (oval), 0.0623 (s-bend) and 0.0616 (slalom), against the 0.06 m limit. steering_oscillation stayed low at 0.14 to 0.28, so there is room for more steering gain. Oval finishes improved (3 of 20, mean time 1.89 s), so base_speed 1.3 is not too slow there. Line_loss_events were 1.25, 2.0 and 1.0. On the s-bend they rose from 1.15 at kp 2.0 to 2.0 at kp 2.5, so higher kp may cause overshoot on that track as well as help the oval.

Change. Following the Evaluator's rule (c), I raise controller.kp from 2.5 to 3.0 as the only change. max_error still reaches 0.06 m with steering_oscillation low, so steering authority is still the binding limit. base_speed, kd, ki, sensor_size, weights and line_loss stay fixed so the effect of kp is isolated.

Expected result. max_error should fall toward about 0.058 m on the oval and slalom. The s-bend is the main risk: line_loss_events may rise above 2 if kp overshoots there, and steering_oscillation may rise above 0.3.

Hypotheses and next measurements. (1) If max_error drops below 0.058 m but completion_time exceeds 3 s on the s-bend or slalom, raise base_speed to 1.5 with kp 3.0. (2) If s-bend line_loss_events rise above 2 while max_error does not improve, kp has passed its useful range; return to kp 2.5 and test controller.line_loss = search_right as the only change, per rule (d). (3) If max_error stays at 0.06 m with kp 3.0, the limit is not steering gain alone, and the next lever is kd (raise toward 0.5 if steering_oscillation stays low). I need per-track max_error, line_loss_events, progress, completion_time and steering_oscillation.
